CPS Async Signal Handling

Provides async signal handling using the self-pipe trick. A POSIX signal handler writes the signal number to a pipe, and the event loop reads it and dispatches to registered handlers.

Usage: initSignalHandling() onSignal(SIGINT, proc() = echo "Got SIGINT") let fut = waitForShutdown() runCps(fut) deinitSignalHandling()

Imports

../runtime, ../eventloop

Types

SignalHandler = proc () {.closure, ...gcsafe.}
A callback invoked when a signal is received.

Procs

proc deinitSignalHandling() {....raises: [Exception], tags: [RootEffect],
                              forbids: [].}
Clean up: restore default signal handlers, unregister from the event loop, close the pipe. Completes pending waitForSignal futures. 
proc initSignalHandling() {....raises: [OSError, IOSelectorsException], tags: [],
                            forbids: [].}
Create the self-pipe and register the read end with the event loop. Must be called before any onSignal/waitForSignal calls. 
proc onSignal(sig: cint; handler: SignalHandler) {....raises: [], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}
Register a persistent handler for the given signal. Multiple handlers per signal are supported. The POSIX sigaction is installed on first use. 
proc removeSignalHandlers(sig: cint) {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Remove all handlers for the given signal and restore SIG_DFL. 
proc waitForShutdown(): CpsVoidFuture {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Returns a future that completes when SIGINT or SIGTERM is received. One-shot: handlers are removed after the first signal fires. 
proc waitForSignal(sig: cint): CpsVoidFuture {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Returns a future that completes when the given signal is received. One-shot: the handler is removed after the signal fires.
